passage.text: When people hear the name "Audubon," they think of birds. That is because a man named John James Audubon was a famous American ornithologist. Ornithologists study birds. But Audubon did not just study birds; he also drew and painted them. He created a stunning collection of life-sized pictures of American birds in the 1800s. His work brought attention to many unknown bird species.

Even as a child, Audubon loved birds. He started drawing them when he was growing up in the French countryside. He continued his hobby when he moved to America in 1803. At his Pennsylvania home, he was the first to "band" birds. He tied strings to the legs of a pair of nesting birds to see if the same pair would return in the spring. They did! Today, bird banding is how scientists track and study migratory birds.

When Audubon moved to the western frontier, he drew and painted the amazing bird species he found there, too. However, it was still just a hobby. But when hard times hit in 1819, Audubon started giving art lessons to earn money. He was also paid to create nature exhibits for a museum. Encouraged by others, he formed a plan to document America's birdlife. He wanted to create a great work of science and art.

Audubon succeeded in his goal, but it did not happen quickly. It took him five years to complete the first few hundred paintings. Then, he toured Europe, exhibiting his paintings and selling subscriptions for prints of them. Many people signed up for the prints he was making. They paid to have sets of five large prints sent to them as each set was completed. People had to wait a long time for all of their prints to arrive. It took ten years in total to complete the entire collection of 435 paintings. The complete work is called Birds of America.

Audubon's work is considered an American masterpiece. His paintings are exhibited in museums around the world. Complete sets of his prints are worth millions of dollars. But the true value of Audubon's work is how it helped people understand and treasure America's birds. The National Audubon Society, created in 1886, still works to conserve and protect America's birds in his name.

passage.text: Imagine a world where no birds sing in the springtime—a silent spring. That is what Rachel Carson asked people to do in her 1962 book, Silent Spring. Carson was sounding an alarm. She was telling people to pay attention to what was happening to the environment.

Born in 1907, Carson grew up on a farm in Pennsylvania. Her two loves were nature and writing. These interests would follow her throughout her life. In college, Carson studied biology and zoology, the sciences of living things and animals. She also wrote for her college newspaper.

After college, Carson went to work as a biologist for the U.S. government. She wrote about fish for an educational radio program. She also wrote newspaper articles, magazine articles, and three popular books about life in the oceans. Her work with the U.S. government lasted for several years.

In the 1950s, Carson became worried about the growing use of pesticides. Pesticides are chemicals that kill pests, like insects that damage crops. One of these pesticides was DDT. People were spraying large amounts of DDT from the air onto crops. Carson learned that DDT was poisoning the food chain. It did not just kill bugs. It also harmed the fish that ate them. And the birds who ate the fish then also became poisoned. For example, Carson found that DDT was causing bald eagle populations across the country to decrease. It took her years to gather her facts, but when she published Silent Spring in 1962, it woke people up to the dangers of overusing pesticides.

The chemical companies that made DDT fought against the facts in Carson's book. But Carson defended her work before Congress. Her book sold over two million copies and started an American environmental movement. People all over the country became interested in helping the environment. Carson's book helped encourage President Richard Nixon to create the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) in 1970. The EPA makes rules to protect people and the environment from pollution. The EPA banned DDT in 1973. After DDT was no longer allowed, the number of bald eagles and other birds started to grow again. These changes happened after Carson's death, but it was her work and love for the planet that sparked a movement that continues today.

However, few other Americans were able to enjoy the cool treat. You needed a special machine to make ice cream, which was churned by hand. Finally, in 1851, Jacob Fussell found a way to make ice cream more easily.

Fussell had been a seller of milk and cream in York, Pennsylvania. He often found, however, that he was left with extra cream. He came up with a way to use the surplus before it turned sour. He decided to turn it into ice cream—lots of it! Months later, the country's first ice cream factory was born in Seven Valleys, Pennsylvania. The factory used machines to churn the ice cream, making it cheaper and easier to produce the frozen treat. Soon, thousands of quarts of ice cream were being shipped by train to Baltimore, Maryland. From there, the ice cream was delivered by trucks to small stores. Then, the shopkeepers sold the ice cream by the scoop to happy customers.

Fussell soon found that running his business in two different states was difficult. So, he moved his factory to Baltimore. He thought it would be simpler to make the ice cream in the same place that he was selling it. He also thought he could save some money since he did not have to ship the ice cream from Pennsylvania. This helped make the cost of ice cream even cheaper, and it helped make ice cream even more popular in the Northeast. Other people saw Fussell's success, and they decided to open up their own factories. Soon, there were ice cream factories around the country.

Today, Jacob Fussell is sometimes called the Father of the Ice Cream Business. There are now over one hundred thousand ice cream and frozen yogurt shops in the United States. In fact, the average American eats about twenty-three pounds of ice cream every year! All of this is thanks to the efforts of Fussell and his ice cream business.

However, few other Americans were able to enjoy the cool treat. You needed a special machine to make ice cream, which was churned by hand. Finally, in 1851, Jacob Fussell found a way to make ice cream more easily.

Fussell had been a seller of milk and cream in York, Pennsylvania. He often found, however, that he was left with extra cream. He came up with a way to use the surplus before it turned sour. He decided to turn it into ice cream—lots of it! Months later, the country's first ice cream factory was born in Seven Valleys, Pennsylvania. The factory used machines to churn the ice cream, making it cheaper and easier to produce the frozen treat. Soon, thousands of quarts of ice cream were being shipped by train to Baltimore, Maryland. From there, the ice cream was delivered by trucks to small stores. Then, the shopkeepers sold the ice cream by the scoop to happy customers.

Fussell soon found that running his business in two different states was difficult. So, he moved his factory to Baltimore. He thought it would be simpler to make the ice cream in the same place that he was selling it. He also thought he could save some money since he did not have to ship the ice cream from Pennsylvania. This helped make the cost of ice cream even cheaper, and it helped make ice cream even more popular in the Northeast. Other people saw Fussell's success, and they decided to open up their own factories. Soon, there were ice cream factories around the country.

Today, Jacob Fussell is sometimes called the Father of the Ice Cream Business. There are now over one hundred thousand ice cream and frozen yogurt shops in the United States. In fact, the average American eats about twenty-three pounds of ice cream every year! All of this is thanks to the efforts of Fussell and his ice cream business.

passage.text: Dolores Huerta is known for her courage, determination, and dedication to improving the lives of others. Huerta is an American activist. An activist is someone who fights for people's rights. Huerta has fought hard for most of her life to improve the working conditions of many people.

Growing up, Huerta watched her mother work tirelessly at her job and in the community. After many years of saving money, Huerta's mother bought a hotel where she offered rooms at a low cost. If someone wasn't able to pay, she often let them stay for free. Dolores Huerta, inspired by her mother's work, joined community service clubs at school and became a Girl Scout. As an adult, Huerta worked as a teacher. When students came to school hungry or without shoes, Huerta felt powerless. She wanted to make a difference, so she began working with a group called the Community Service Organization. They helped support Mexican-American communities.

To continue her efforts helping those in need, she and others created the National Farm Workers Association (NFWA). Its purpose was to support California farmworkers who often worked long hours without breaks, bathrooms, drinking water, or fair pay. When the NFWA became the United Farm Workers (UFW), Huerta served as vice president. In this role, she talked with farm owners about fair pay and making the farmworkers' jobs safe. She helped the workers get better pay and protection.

For example, in 1965, many grape growers in California were treating their workers poorly. In order to push the growers to make changes, Huerta and others organized a boycott. She encouraged people across the country to stop buying grapes. This made the grape growers lose money. The Delano Grape Strike lasted for five years, and eventually, the growers decided to pay their workers more. Safety for workers in the fields also improved, including increased protection against harmful chemicals called pesticides. During her time in the UFW, Huerta created the popular saying "Sí, se puede." This translates to "Yes, you can." This phrase encourages people to work toward their goals without giving up.

In 2002, Huerta started the Dolores Huerta Foundation. One of its goals is to help people become active in their communities. In 2012, Huerta won the Presidential Medal of Freedom. This award is given by the President and is one of the highest honors that an American citizen can receive. It is one of many awards Huerta has won. On April 10 each year, the people of California celebrate Dolores Huerta Day to honor and celebrate her life.

Mister Rogers' Neighborhood had puppets, storytelling, and music. Each show began with Rogers entering the house where his show was filmed. Inside his home was a small make-believe neighborhood.
